recentItems.title: US workers head back to school to reskill as AI reshapes the job market
recentItems.description:
Around the world, economists and workers alike are concerned about AI replacing humans.
A recent report from the McKinsey Global Institute found that roughly 11 million American workers, or about 7 percent of the workforce, may need to switch jobs in less than a decade. 

Al Jazeera’s John Hendren reports from Los Angeles, where some workers are doing something about it.

recentItems.title: Why does Europe want to erase its Muslim history? | Tariq Ali | Deja Vu
recentItems.description:
From Spain to Sicily, Muslims helped shape Europe for centuries. Why do they still seem to be cast as outsiders? In this episode of Deja Vu, author Tariq Ali traces the rise of al-Andalus to its fall amid the burning of books and the loss of a shared past. How does that history still shape Europe’s politics today?

In this episode: 

- Tariq Ali, author and editor of the New Left Review

recentItems.title: Lula and Flavio Bolsonaro face off in tightly contested Brazil election
recentItems.description:
Polls have just opened in Brazil, for one of the most tightly contested elections in the country's history. 
The incumbent president, Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, is running for a fourth non-consecutive term.
His main rival is far-right senator, Flavio Bolsonaro, son of the former president, Jair Bolsonaro.
159 million voters are eligible to choose not only a president, but state governors as well as federal and state representatives.

Al Jazeera’s Lucia Newman reports from Sao Paulo, Brazil

recentItems.title: S Korea teaches AI in primary schools in bid to become a global superpower
recentItems.description:
South Korea is investing almost $900bn to rival China and the US as an AI superpower.
To ensure enough home-grown talent, primary school children are taught robotics and how to code.
They're also taught to question the ethics of the technology they're building.  

Al Jazeera’s Jack Barton reports from Seoul, South Korea on what students are learning, and why teachers say there's no turning back.

recentItems.title: Brief: US sending more troops to Middle East even as it withdraws from Iraq | The Take

recentItems.title: Flydubai: What happens when a plane plunges 17,000 feet? | AJ #shorts
recentItems.description:
A flight instructor recreates the Flydubai jet’s near-vertical 17,000 foot dive in a simulator. He says the plane would have exceeded its maximum structural speed, and that anything unsecured would have flown all over the cabin during the recovery’s negative G-forces.

recentItems.title: Somalia’s only special needs school faces closure amid funding cuts
recentItems.description:
The only school dedicated to children with special needs in Somalia’s capital is at risk of closing.
The Mustaqbal Centre for Special Needs provides free education to more than 140 children, 70% of whom have been diagnosed with autism.
Government funding covers only part of its costs and private donations have fallen sharply amid rising prices and energy costs.

Al Jazeera’s Nicolas Haque reports.

recentItems.title: US proposal focuses on nuclear issue, but Iran's focus is on Strait of Hormuz: Baghaei
recentItems.description:
Iran’s Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei addresses US war in press conference in Tehran.

The top issue being discussed by Iran is the reopening of the critical Strait of Hormuz, its Foreign Ministry spokesperson says.

“We are at this stage focusing on the strait foremost, and our main concern is to reach a solution and to have peace and stability restored within this waterway,” Esmaeil Baghaei said.

“However, certain tangible measures must be taken by the United States. Certain issues were put to discussions. Iran sees attempts to violate or interrupt the memorandum of understanding in addition to the other issues that have arisen in the past few months. Above all the sanctions imposed by the United States must be lifted.”

Al Jazeera's Mohamed Vall reports from Tehran, Iran.
